Dai et al. use loopless cyclic graphs with zero-allowed support, `B_ji ≠ 0 ⇒ i→j`, invertible `I−B`, and mutually independent, nonconstant, non-Gaussian sources; they impose neither centering nor finite moments. Their graphical theorem is stated for irreducible models after a reduction step. The present note instead uses exact support, fixed latent cardinality, centered finite-variance sources, and intervention-wise solvability, so it does not presently use Dai et al.’s published class. [Dai et al., §2 and Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.04780v1)

The current headline cannot simply be relabeled or transferred upward by inclusion: equality or separation of exact-support strata is not monotone under enlarging both graph law sets, and `thm:strict-interventional-refinement` explicitly fails at zero pivots. There is, however, a material missed elbow. For the same fixed node set,

    P^≤_I(G) = ⋃_{F⊆G} P^=_I(F).

Therefore zero-allowed containment has an exact finite criterion: for every `F⊆G` and `C∈D_F`, some `K⊆H` and one `(D,f,a)` must satisfy the existing source-partition and simultaneous-response equations. This is only a finite downward-closure disjunction, remains decidable by the existing compiler, and directly extends the anchor class to joint interventions. The population result can also drop centering and finite moments: the mixture proof already uses admissible Bernoulli diagnostics and Cramér decomposition, while equality of response slopes follows from rigidity of probability laws under nonzero translations rather than means. Finite moments should remain local to `thm:strict-interventional-refinement` and the inference rung.
